items.title: Joe Temperley interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 11, 1997
items.q: The interviewee discusses the Basie band's stability and prestige compared to other bands, but does not mention a personal connection, employment, or collaboration with Count Basie himself.

ctx.x: Well the band was different then. I mean they were on a mission. The band was entirely different. Mercer’s band wasn’t like that at all. Half the people in the band didn’t know anything about Duke Ellington. So it was a different thing. And then when the Ellington band was in its prime, of course, the musicians couldn’t work in the studios in New York, because of the racial thing. So that’s why the Basie band was together all the time and that’s why the Ellington band was together. And that’s why the Basie band…
So for the black musicians playing with Ellington or Basie was the height.
That was a career in itself. That was as good as you could get. Of course that made the band great. © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -9-
